A flight through a field of turning blocks, lit by the track. The spectrum sets them alight and the camera re-frames itself every few bars.
A flower of light on a golden spiral. Around the wheel is frequency, outward from the heart is time, so every beat opens at the centre and travels out through the petals.

Sand on a sounding plate, as Chladni did it in 1787. The grains flee wherever the plate moves and settle on the lines where it stands still, so the figure is the music itself. In silence the sand simply stops.

The spectrum, mirrored into four. Bass sits in the middle and treble runs out to the edges. Each band\'s level draws a dark line with the light opening away from it, so loud bands glow wide and quiet ones close to a seam.

A tunnel of folded light, flown to the beat. The camera cuts every two bars and the walls change shape on the phrase, so the edit follows the record instead of a clock. Analysed tracks drive it from their own beat grid.

Two mirrors, set at an angle, with a single strut between them. Reflecting it four times over builds a rose window, and the record sets the angle: the pattern comes round a different number of times on every phrase.

A slice through a grid that has four dimensions instead of three. Nothing in the grid moves. The beat moves the slice, so cells swell out of nothing, open and close again, and every phrase turns the grid in a direction that has no equivalent here.
